say: Eighty-five thousand documents.
One question.
And an answer that sounds completely certain.
Meet the deceptive witness.
Evidence that looks like support, but isn't.
Two citations agree, until you trace them back to one original.
An incident report describes the past. It does not authorize the present.
And a runbook from twenty twenty-four still speaks with a confidence it no longer has.
QualityRag answers with a contract.
A PackSpec declares what any answer must prove: each requirement, how many independent sources, and how fresh they must be.
It is versioned, and the same contract runs in ten languages.
No language model decides whether the evidence is enough.
Every check ends in one of three verdicts.
Admit.
Inconclusive.
Refuse.
When proof is missing, the answer is withheld, and the gap is named.
And admit means the declared checks passed. Not that the source is true.

steps.say: This is not a mockup. It is the live engine, checking a real policy.
Remove one memo, and the verdict changes.
Not enough evidence. The gap is named.

say: But a contract is only as good as the knowledge behind it.
So QualityRag grows a Semantic Garden: an append-only research tree.
People and AI agents propose, challenge, test, and synthesize.
Nothing is ever deleted.
A pruned branch can be reopened, when new evidence arrives.
Candidates compete with the champion on fresh, held-out families, under the same PackSpec.
The winner is promoted. The other is kept, because a counterexample is knowledge.
That is the loop: find failure, investigate, propose, test, retain, and promote, or reopen.
Evidence before answers.
QualityRag. Start with the Academy, or read the code.
